title: Cloud sessions, self-hosted: remote machines over an SSH tunnel
request: The owner's goal: Claude Code's and Codex's capabilities; for cloud sessions the owner chose 'one of my SSH machines: DCLab Code runs the agent there and shows it here'.
plan: Connect opens an SSH tunnel and the remote DCLab Code's page here
the agent never drives the remote one

decisions.decision: run DCLab Code itself on the person's machine and reach its page through a tunnel, not a new remote protocol
decisions.why: everything (guards, records, caps) already works in DCLab Code; the tunnel adds only the way in

decisions.decision: keys or the ssh agent only (BatchMode), never a password
decisions.why: the app never handles the person's secrets

decisions.decision: tunnel ends in a fixed port range (47100-47199) that the agent's guards treat as the person's
decisions.why: a static range keeps the guards simple and covers a tunnel the app lost track of

change: dclab-code server/remote.js (new), server/app.js (settings remotes, /api/remotes/connect|disconnect, tunnels closed with the app), server/preview_tool.js and server/config.js (the tunnel range guarded), web/* (the Remote machines section), tests/fixtures/fake-ssh.mjs, tests, docs/REMOTE.md.

findings.defect: two Connects at once left an ssh nothing could close
findings.scenario: Connect clicked in the Mac app and a browser tab together
findings.cause: the tunnel was recorded only after an await; the second overwrote the first
findings.fix: a per-machine connect under way: a second click waits for it
findings.test: unit test: two connects, one tunnel, nothing answering after closeAll; undoing the fix fails it

findings.defect: an old failing connect killed a newer good one; a connect during the wait reported success early
findings.scenario: wrong port, Disconnect, right port within 20 s
findings.cause: the failure path disconnected by name; reuse did not wait for readiness
findings.fix: a failure closes only its own tunnel; only a ready tunnel is reused
findings.test: unit test; undoing the fix fails it

findings.defect: the tunnel's port escaped the agent's guards
findings.scenario: the agent finds the port with ps, curls the remote page for its token and drives the remote DCLab Code's person-only acts
findings.cause: the guards listed fixed ports only
findings.fix: tunnels use 47100-47199; the preview refuses it and the person rule asks for shell or fetch to it
findings.test: unit tests on guardCheck and the preview's allowed()

findings.defect: the guide said the tunnel was the only door
findings.scenario: on a shared server another user curls 127.0.0.1:4317 and drives the agent with the person's key
findings.cause: 127.0.0.1 keeps out the internet, not the machine's other users
findings.fix: the guide says: only a machine where you are the only user

findings.defect: a shared ControlMaster could keep the forward after Disconnect
findings.cause: the forward lives in the master

findings.defect: a tunnel killed from outside still showed connected and was reused
findings.scenario: the ssh process killed from outside (pkill ssh, out of memory)
findings.test: unit test kills it from outside; undoing the fix fails it (the first version of the test killed it from inside and passed on broken code)

findings.scenario: a remote port redirecting to this app's own page

findings.cause: the log line came after the throw
findings.fix: every attempt logged with ok and the error

measurements.name: tests
measurements.gate: every test passes; each fix's test fails when the fix is undone
measurements.result: dclab-code 120 of 120; a second DCLab Code as the remote, a session started through the tunnel ran there

measurements.name: mac smoke
measurements.gate: the app opens and its page script runs with no error

outcome: DCLab Code has cloud sessions on the person's own machine: Connect, its DCLab Code here, sessions running there while the laptop sleeps.
lessons: A test that kills a process from inside proves nothing about a kill from outside.
Loopback keeps out the internet, not the machine's other users: say who can reach it.
risks: not yet run against a real SSH server (waits on the owner's host)
R&D's store does not read a remote machine's records
